title: Ethiopian Easter Doro Wat
localName: ፋሲካ ዶሮ ወጥ — Fasika Doro Wat
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — the Easter celebration Doro Wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Easter Doro Wat — the Doro Wat prepared specifically for Fasika (Easter), made with extra berbere, extra kibbeh, three hours of slow simmering, and 12 eggs (one per apostle). The greatest expression of Doro Wat — made after the 55-day Lenten fast, the first meat meal of Easter morning.
longDesc: Fasika Doro Wat is Doro Wat at its absolute pinnacle — the version made after 55 days of fasting (the Ethiopian Orthodox Great Lent), when meat has not been consumed for nearly two months. The anticipation drives the cook to exceed themselves: more berbere, more kibbeh, longer simmering, more eggs. The chicken is cut into exactly 12 pieces. The eggs number 12. The sauce must be so thick it barely pours. This is the most important meal of the Ethiopian year.
ingredients: 2 whole chickens (3 kg total) — cut into 12 pieces each
// Marinade: 6 tbsp lemon juice, 3 tsp salt
12 hard-boiled eggs — pierced very deeply all over
steps: Marinate both chickens in lemon and salt — 1 hour. Rinse. Pat dry.
Dry caramelise the onions — 35 minutes of patient stirring, no oil.
Add kibbeh. Melt and combine. Cook 4 minutes.
Add berbere. Toast in the kibbeh 6 minutes — the sauce should be deeply red.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste. Cook 3 minutes.
Add all chicken pieces. Coat every single piece.
Add water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to lowest possible heat. Cover. Simmer 2 hours.
Pierce the eggs with a skewer — 15—20 deep holes per egg.
Add eggs. Simmer covered 30 more minutes.
The sauce must be very thick, deeply red, and clinging to the chicken.
chefTips: Fasika Doro Wat is always made the day before — the overnight resting is essential.
The eggs must be pierced more deeply than for regular Doro Wat — use a skewer, not just a fork.
35 minutes of dry-caramelised onions — the extra time produces more depth.
8 tablespoons of berbere — this is Fasika, the greatest day.
This is the only day of the year when the sauce can never be too thick or too red.
commonMistakes: Making on the day — must be made the day before.
cookingScience: See ETH061 for Doro Wat cooking science. Fasika Doro Wat's extended cooking (3 hours vs 2.5) converts more collagen to gelatin and concentrates the sauce to a higher viscosity. The additional berbere means more carotenoids dissolved in the kibbeh — producing a more intensely red colour and more complex flavour.
storage: Refrigerate 5 days. Freeze 3 months. Must be made the day before.
healthBenefits: After 55 days of fasting, this meal provides the most complete protein replenishment possible.
The berbere's iron is particularly welcome after the legume-heavy fasting diet.
culturalNote: Fasika Doro Wat is the food of resurrection — prepared after 55 days of abstinence, cooked through the night before Easter, served as the first meal after the overnight Easter service. Every Ethiopian Orthodox Christian knows the feeling of eating this Doro Wat after weeks of fasting — it is one of the most emotionally powerful food experiences in the world. The smell of it cooking is the smell of Easter morning.
